newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares at the whim of dollar in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares at the whim of dollar in slow trade.

text.p: German shares will remain mostly at the whim of the dollar in the near-term as the market searched for fresh fundamental data to support another run at record levels, traders said on Thursday.
"The DAX index is rising and falling with the dollar," said one Frankfurt trader.
The DAX index, keying off the dollar trading below 1.69 marks, fell 11.58 points to 3,562.11 points, while the IBIS DAX extended the drop to 3,557.88 points.
Range trade is expected for the rest of Thursday and ahead of Friday's expiry of DAX and stock option futures.
Another factor keeping the market in check is next Tuesday's FOMC meeting and speculation on whether the Federal Reserve may opt to raise U.S. interest rates.
"There's not much room for movement right now and it looks as though we are going to be locked in somewhat volatile range trade," said one Frankfurt dealer.
Carmakers, hurt by the weaker dollar, were steady to lower despite the VDA German automobile association reporting a 15 percent year-on-year rise in vehicle production.
Volkswagen AG ended down four marks at 1,149 marks and Daimler-Benz AG was down 10 pfennigs at 134.20 marks.

BMW AG ended bourse trade down 35 marks at 1,430 marks despite the Munich-based carmaker reporting on Thursday a provisional 17.4 percent rise in five-month sales to 24.3 billion marks and a nearly eight percent rise in vehicle deliveries to 497,000 for the period from January to May.
Chemical shares were mixed despite the weaker dollar.
BASF AG fell despite saying 1997 sales would top 50 billion marks and that sales and profits would remain at high levels in the coming months. BASF shares fell 17 pfennigs to 67.28 marks.
But rival Hoechst AG rose 15 pfennigs to 65.85 marks and Bayer AG rose 25 pfennigs to 65.20 marks.
